classification.difficultyReason: Sketch horizontal and vertical translations of a supplied graph, including two combined translations.

content.prompt:
Assume that each grid in this exercise is composed of squares with side length one unit.

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below. Sketch the graphs of:

spec.description: Unit grid with four squares across and vertically, perpendicular axes with positive arrowheads, x and y labels, and no numerical tick labels. Blue joined segments have closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (-1,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), in that order. Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no transformed answers.

answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit left: $(x,y)\mapsto(x-1,y)$. Join the image points $(-2,-1)$, $(-1,1)$ and $(0,-1)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1(a); teacher PDF page 32, Section C 1(a)
spec.description: Complete translated graph on a unit grid, with source axis labels and closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (-2,-1), (-1,1), (0,-1). Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.

answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit right: $(x,y)\mapsto(x+1,y)$. Join the image points $(0,-1)$, $(1,1)$ and $(2,-1)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1(b); teacher PDF page 32, Section C 1(b)
spec.description: Complete translated graph on a unit grid, with source axis labels and closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (0,-1), (1,1), (2,-1). Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.

answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit up: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+1)$. Join the image points $(-1,0)$, $(0,2)$ and $(1,0)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1(c); teacher PDF page 32, Section C 1(c)
spec.description: Complete translated graph on a unit grid, with source axis labels and closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (-1,0), (0,2), (1,0). Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.

answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit down: $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y-1)$. Join the image points $(-1,-2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,-2)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1(d); teacher PDF page 32, Section C 1(d)
spec.description: Complete translated graph on a unit grid, with source axis labels and closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (-1,-2), (0,0), (1,-2). Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.

answer.short:
Join $(0,0)$, $(1,2)$ and $(2,0)$ in order.

Translate 1 unit right and 1 unit up.
answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit right and 1 unit up: $(x,y)\mapsto(x+1,y+1)$. Join the image points $(0,0)$, $(1,2)$ and $(2,0)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1(e); teacher PDF page 32, Section C 1(e)
spec.description: Complete graph after both translations on a unit grid, with source axis labels and closed outer endpoints.
spec.mathematics: Join (0,0), (1,2), (2,0). Grid step is 1; both axes span -2 to 2.

answer.short:
Join $(-2,-2)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,-2)$ in order.

Translate 1 unit left and 1 unit down.
answer.worked: Translate the graph 1 unit left and 1 unit down: $(x,y)\mapsto(x-1,y-1)$. Join the image points $(-2,-2)$, $(-1,0)$ and $(0,-2)$ with straight segments, retaining closed outer endpoints.
